answer.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure creates urgency to respond, but memory_73 and exp_73 conclusively show that promotional pricing drives acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention (-12%) and fails to retain at renewal. This directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) work for established customers but do not address immediate churn of price-sensitive accounts. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is valuable but does not stem SMB churn. The optimal response leverages three high-confidence, low-risk learnings: (1) activation_messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action; (2) simplified onboarding (memory_31, memory_86) improved activation and retention; (3) both preserve time-to-value and engagement without discounting, creating defensive stickiness against price-based defection. A standard_experiment rolling out enhanced activation messaging + streamlined onboarding flows to at-risk SMB cohorts addresses the immediate churn driver (value realization) rather than competing on price. This protects long-term revenue quality and renewal rates while neutralizing the competitor's short-term advantage. No material downstream value risk; these levers have documented positive retention impact.
